title: Sashimi Omakase Platter

seo.title: How to Make Sashimi Omakase Platter — Easy Japanese Recipe
seo.metaDescription: Learn how to make authentic Sashimi Omakase Platter. This easy Japanese recipe includes step-by-step instructions, tips, and serving ideas for a delightful seafood experience.

description: An Omakase Sashimi Platter is a chef's selection of the freshest seasonal seafood, expertly sliced and beautifully presented. This recipe guides you through creating your own exquisite array of raw fish, highlighting delicate flavors and textures. It's a true culinary art form that celebrates the ocean's bounty.

ingredients.notes: sashimi block, preferably Akami or Chutoro
freshly grated or good quality paste
high quality, light soy sauce recommended

instructions.title: Prepare Your Workspace and Fish
instructions.text: Ensure your cutting board, knives, and hands are impeccably clean. Rinse all sushi-grade fish blocks under cold water, pat them completely dry with paper towels, and place them on a clean tray. Keep them chilled until ready to slice. Prepare a bowl of ice water for chilling the sliced fish if needed.

instructions.title: Prepare Accompaniments and Garnish
instructions.text: Julienne the daikon radish very thinly and place it in ice water to crisp up. Arrange pickled ginger and wasabi artfully on small serving dishes or directly on the main platter. Thinly slice the lemon for garnish. Wash and pat dry the shiso leaves.

instructions.title: Slice the Tuna (Maguro)
instructions.text: Using a very sharp, long sashimi knife (yanagiba), slice the tuna against the grain into uniform pieces, about 1/4 inch thick. Use a single, smooth pulling motion for each slice. Arrange the slices neatly on a chilled serving platter as you go.

instructions.title: Slice the Salmon (Sake) and Yellowtail (Hamachi)
instructions.text: Repeat the slicing process for the salmon and yellowtail. Salmon can be sliced slightly thicker if desired. For yellowtail, aim for similar thickness to tuna. Arrange these alongside the tuna, creating an appealing color contrast on your platter.

instructions.title: Prepare Scallops and Uni
instructions.text: If using whole scallops, slice them horizontally into 2-3 discs. Gently pat them dry. Carefully spoon the fresh sea urchin (uni) onto a shiso leaf or directly onto the platter. Handle uni with extreme care to maintain its delicate texture and appearance.

instructions.title: Assemble and Garnish the Platter
instructions.text: Drain the julienned daikon radish and pat dry. Arrange the daikon, shiso leaves, and lemon slices around and among the sashimi. Ensure enough space for each type of fish to be appreciated. The key is aesthetic balance and freshness. Serve immediately with small bowls of soy sauce for dipping.

tips: Always use the freshest, highest quality sushi-grade fish from a reputable supplier. This is the most critical factor for delicious and safe sashimi.
Invest in a very sharp, high-quality sashimi knife. A clean, single-motion cut prevents tearing the delicate fish flesh, preserving its texture and appearance.
Keep all ingredients, especially the fish, very cold until just before serving. A chilled platter or serving over ice can help maintain freshness throughout the meal.
